from.place: set-of-representatives proof, affine case: a perfect object on Spec A comes from a bounded complex of finite projective A-modules

title: Perfect objects on an affine scheme are bounded finite projective complexes
statement: Let $A$ be a ring and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme]. An object $E$ of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-category] is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex] if and only if $E$ is isomorphic in $D(\mathcal O_Y)$ to $\widetilde{P^\bullet}$ for a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite projective $A$-modules.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma perfect-lemma-perfect-affine (Tag 08EB), with More on Algebra, Definition 0656 (a perfect object of D(A) is one isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective A-modules)

proof.text: Obtain an affine equivalence e and a pseudo-coherent finite-Tor preimage C by [lem-pc-perfect-affine-module-preimage]. Apply [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect] to get P and Q(P) ≅ C. Apply e and the inclusion to this isomorphism, invert it, and compose with E ≅ e(C) and the natural tilde comparison at P. This gives the forward implication with the unchanged bounds and finite/projective witnesses.

Given E ≅ Q(tilde(P)), [lem-pc-affine-projective-local-strict-model] gives a strict model K on each neighborhood U. Map the given isomorphism through derived restriction and compose with the model comparison, producing exactly the witness required by [def-pc-perfect-complex].

proof_origin.place: Tag 08EB, reduced to affine finite-Tor preimage and local strict-model comparison; existing ring criterion applied in Lean
